A makes key operations and health status easy to scan at a glance; B requires interpretation because important content is missing, underemphasized, or visually disconnected.

It provides a clear workspace structure with sidebar organization, content hierarchy, and obvious note actions, so users can understand where notes live and how to work with them immediately. A is extremely incomplete: it shows only a title and one button on a largely empty canvas, with no visible organization, categorization, or note-taking structure, which hard-caps its UX across all dimensions.
key_differences: B presents a complete note-taking layout with sidebar categories and a readable content pane, while A is mostly empty and lacks any note structure.
B matches the requested Notion-like classroom notes scenario through navigation, sections, and content organization; A does not demonstrate categorization beyond a generic Add Section button.
B has clearer hierarchy and scanability with page title, section headings, lists, and tables; A provides almost no information path or task context.
